paragraphs.title: The Growth of Humanity and the Nephilim

easy.question: What happened when people began to multiply on the earth?
answers: Daughters were born to them
A tower was built
The flood began
easy.explanation: The verse says, “and daughters were born to them.”

easy.question: Who saw the daughters of men?
answers: The Nephilim
The sons of God
The men of renown
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the sons of God saw the daughters of men.”

easy.question: How many years were appointed for human life?
answers: Seventy years
Two hundred years
One hundred and twenty years
easy.explanation: The verse says, “his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.”

medium.question: What happened first according to the order of the verses?
answers: People multiplied and daughters were born
The Nephilim were called men of renown
Human life was limited to 120 years
medium.explanation: First, people multiplied and daughters were born; afterward, the sons of God saw them and took them as wives.

medium.question: What does the phrase “for that he also is flesh” mean in context?
answers: Although he is spirit
Because he is also flesh
When he becomes mighty
medium.explanation: The phrase explains that human beings are limited because they are flesh.

medium.question: What is the connection between God’s words in verse 3 and the length of human life?
answers: Life became unlimited
Humanity ceased to exist
A limit of 120 years was established
medium.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.”

challenge.question: What can be understood from the words “and also after that” regarding the Nephilim?
answers: They were on the earth during a later period as well
They appeared only after the flood
They disappeared before that time
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the Nephilim were on the earth in those days and also afterward, describing their presence in two periods.

challenge.question: What does “of all which they chose” suggest about the choice of wives?
answers: The women made the choice alone
The sons of God chose broadly, without a specific limit stated in the verse
They chose only women from their own families
challenge.explanation: The phrase presents a broad choice according to their desire.

challenge.question: How does the verse describe the children born to the sons of God and the daughters of men?
answers: As weak people
As holy priests
As mighty men and men of renown
challenge.explanation: The verse says they became “mighty men, which were of old, men of renown.”

questions.question: What can be understood from the words “and also after that” regarding the Nephilim?
answers: They were on the earth during a later period as well
They appeared only after the flood
They disappeared before that time
questions.explanation: The verse says that the Nephilim were on the earth in those days and also afterward, describing their presence in two periods.

questions.question: What does “of all which they chose” suggest about the choice of wives?
answers: The women made the choice alone
The sons of God chose broadly, without a specific limit stated in the verse
They chose only women from their own families
questions.explanation: The phrase presents a broad choice according to their desire.

questions.question: How does the verse describe the children born to the sons of God and the daughters of men?
answers: As weak people
As holy priests
As mighty men and men of renown
questions.explanation: The verse says they became “mighty men, which were of old, men of renown.”

paragraphs.title: Human Wickedness and the Decision to Destroy

easy.question: What did the Lord see among the people on the earth?
answers: That their wickedness was great
That everyone was righteous
That the earth was empty
easy.explanation: The verse says that “the wickedness of man was great in the earth.”

easy.question: What did the Lord say he would do to humanity and the animals?
answers: Bless them
Destroy them from the face of the earth
Lead them to another land
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth,” and also mentioned the animals.

easy.question: Who found grace in the eyes of the Lord?
answers: The first man
All humanity
Noah
easy.explanation: The passage ends by saying, “Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.”

medium.question: Why did the Lord decide to destroy humanity and the animals?
answers: Because wickedness and evil thoughts were widespread and continual
Because no animals remained on the earth
Because Noah asked him to do so
medium.explanation: The decision followed humanity’s wickedness and the fact that the thoughts of the heart were continually evil.

medium.question: What happened before the Lord said, “I will destroy man”?
answers: Noah found grace in his eyes
The Lord regretted making man
The animals left the earth
medium.explanation: First the Lord saw the evil, then he regretted making man, and then he announced the destruction.

medium.question: In the phrase “I will destroy man whom I have created,” what does “destroy” mean?
answers: I will bless
I will invite
I will wipe out or remove
medium.explanation: The context shows that the Lord intended to remove humanity from the face of the earth.

challenge.question: What does the list of creatures the Lord wanted to destroy—man, beast, creeping thing, and fowl—show?
answers: The judgment was broad and not limited to human beings
Only birds were guilty
The Lord wanted to destroy only Noah
challenge.explanation: The list shows that the destruction concerned the animal world as well as humanity.

challenge.question: What is the main contrast between verses 7 and 8?
answers: Noah is punished in verse 7, and praised in verse 8
Despite the decision to destroy the world, Noah found grace in the Lord’s eyes
Animals are saved in verse 7 and disappear in verse 8
challenge.explanation: Verse 7 describes judgment and destruction, while verse 8 presents Noah as an exception who found grace.

challenge.question: What does “only” emphasize in the phrase “every imagination ... was only evil continually”?
answers: The evil appeared only at night
The evil belonged only to a few people
The thoughts were exclusively and continually evil
challenge.explanation: “Only” excludes goodness, while “continually” emphasizes that the evil persisted.

questions.question: What does the list of creatures the Lord wanted to destroy—man, beast, creeping thing, and fowl—show?
answers: The judgment was broad and not limited to human beings
Only birds were guilty
The Lord wanted to destroy only Noah
questions.explanation: The list shows that the destruction concerned the animal world as well as humanity.

questions.question: What is the main contrast between verses 7 and 8?
answers: Noah is punished in verse 7, and praised in verse 8
Despite the decision to destroy the world, Noah found grace in the Lord’s eyes
Animals are saved in verse 7 and disappear in verse 8
questions.explanation: Verse 7 describes judgment and destruction, while verse 8 presents Noah as an exception who found grace.

questions.question: What does “only” emphasize in the phrase “every imagination ... was only evil continually”?
answers: The evil appeared only at night
The evil belonged only to a few people
The thoughts were exclusively and continually evil
questions.explanation: “Only” excludes goodness, while “continually” emphasizes that the evil persisted.

paragraphs.title: Righteous Noah and the Corrupt Earth

easy.question: Who is described as a just and perfect man?
answers: Abraham
Noah
Moses
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says that Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations.

easy.question: How many sons did Noah have?
answers: Two
Four
Three
easy.explanation: Verse 10 names Noah’s three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

easy.question: What was the earth filled with?
answers: Violence
Peace
Wisdom
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the earth was filled with violence.”

medium.question: What was the relationship between the corruption of the earth and human behavior?
answers: People corrupted their way, and therefore the earth was corrupt
Noah corrupted the earth
The earth corrupted the people
medium.explanation: The verses explain that the earth was corrupt because all flesh had corrupted its way upon it.

medium.question: In the phrase “the earth was filled with violence,” what does “violence” mean?
answers: Heavy rain
Violence and injustice
Great joy
medium.explanation: In this context, violence refers to wrongdoing, oppression, and injustice.

medium.question: What is described first in these verses: Noah’s righteousness or the corruption of the earth?
answers: The corruption of the earth
Noah’s righteousness
The birth of Noah’s sons
medium.explanation: The passage first describes Noah and his righteousness, then his sons, and afterward the corruption and violence on earth.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “in his generations” about the time Noah lived?
answers: Noah lived in only one generation
Noah lived during a period spanning several generations
Noah lived before the creation of the world
challenge.explanation: The plural phrase refers to the generations among which Noah lived and whose corruption highlighted his righteousness.

challenge.question: In the sentence “all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth,” what does “his way” refer to?
answers: The way of all humanity and living creatures
Noah’s way alone
God’s way alone
challenge.explanation: The sentence concerns “all flesh,” indicating that living beings generally had corrupted their conduct.

challenge.question: What major contrast appears between Noah and the rest of the world?
answers: Noah was rich, while the others were poor
Noah was old, while the others were young
Noah walked with God, while the earth was filled with violence
challenge.explanation: Noah is described as righteous and walking with God, unlike the corrupt and violent world around him.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “in his generations” about the time Noah lived?
answers: Noah lived in only one generation
Noah lived during a period spanning several generations
Noah lived before the creation of the world
questions.explanation: The plural phrase refers to the generations among which Noah lived and whose corruption highlighted his righteousness.

questions.question: In the sentence “all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth,” what does “his way” refer to?
answers: The way of all humanity and living creatures
Noah’s way alone
God’s way alone
questions.explanation: The sentence concerns “all flesh,” indicating that living beings generally had corrupted their conduct.

questions.question: What major contrast appears between Noah and the rest of the world?
answers: Noah was rich, while the others were poor
Noah was old, while the others were young
Noah walked with God, while the earth was filled with violence
questions.explanation: Noah is described as righteous and walking with God, unlike the corrupt and violent world around him.

paragraphs.title: The Command to Build the Ark

easy.question: Why did God say that he would destroy the earth?
answers: Because it had no trees
Because the earth was filled with violence
Because it had no light
easy.explanation: The verse says that the earth was filled with violence, so God would destroy it.

easy.question: What material was Noah commanded to use for the ark?
answers: Gopher wood
Stone
Metal
easy.explanation: God said, “Make thee an ark of gopher wood.”

easy.question: How long was the ark?
answers: Fifty cubits
Thirty cubits
Three hundred cubits
easy.explanation: The verse says that the ark was three hundred cubits long.

medium.question: What was the connection between the violence on earth and God’s command to Noah?
answers: Because of the violence, God announced destruction and commanded Noah to build an ark
Because of the violence, Noah was told only to leave the earth
Because of the violence, the ark was meant to store crops
medium.explanation: The violence was the reason for judgment, and in that context God commanded Noah to prepare an ark.

medium.question: In the phrase “A window shalt thou make to the ark,” what was the window for?
answers: A storeroom
An opening to let in light
A staircase
medium.explanation: The window was an opening in the ark, associated with letting in light.

medium.question: How many levels or stories did the ark have?
answers: One
Two
Three
medium.explanation: The ark had lower, second, and third stories—three levels.

challenge.question: Which numerical conclusion follows from the ark’s dimensions?
answers: Its height was greater than its length
Its width was greater than its length
Its length was six times its width
challenge.explanation: The ark was 300 cubits long and 50 cubits wide, so its length was six times its width.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the command to pitch the ark within and without?
answers: The ark was meant to be completely open
It had to be sealed and protected from water
The ark was made of stone
challenge.explanation: Pitching the ark inside and outside provided sealing and protection against water.

challenge.question: Which accurate detail about the ark’s structure appears in the verses?
answers: The door was in the side, and the window was part of the upper structure
The door was at the bottom, and the ark had no window
The door was only in the roof, and the ark had no levels
challenge.explanation: The verse places the door in the side and also mentions a window and three stories.

questions.question: Which numerical conclusion follows from the ark’s dimensions?
answers: Its height was greater than its length
Its width was greater than its length
Its length was six times its width
questions.explanation: The ark was 300 cubits long and 50 cubits wide, so its length was six times its width.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the command to pitch the ark within and without?
answers: The ark was meant to be completely open
It had to be sealed and protected from water
The ark was made of stone
questions.explanation: Pitching the ark inside and outside provided sealing and protection against water.

questions.question: Which accurate detail about the ark’s structure appears in the verses?
answers: The door was in the side, and the window was part of the upper structure
The door was at the bottom, and the ark had no window
The door was only in the roof, and the ark had no levels
questions.explanation: The verse places the door in the side and also mentions a window and three stories.

paragraphs.title: The Flood and God’s Covenant with Noah

easy.question: What did the Lord bring upon the earth?
answers: A flood of waters
A great fire
A strong wind
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I do bring a flood of waters upon the earth.”

easy.question: What would happen to everything on the earth?
answers: It would be saved
It would die
It would be rebuilt
easy.explanation: The verse says, “every thing that is in the earth shall die.”

easy.question: Who would enter the ark with Noah?
answers: Only his sons
Everyone on earth
His sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives
easy.explanation: The verse lists Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives.

medium.question: Why were Noah and his family told to enter the ark?
answers: To be saved from the flood
To build a new city
To travel through the land
medium.explanation: After announcing the flood, the Lord told Noah and his family to enter the ark for safety.

medium.question: What order of events is described in these verses?
answers: Noah entered the ark, and only afterward did the Lord announce the flood
The Lord announced the flood, established his covenant with Noah, and told him to enter the ark
The Lord made a covenant with everyone on earth, and then the flood stopped
medium.explanation: The Lord first announced the flood, then mentioned his covenant with Noah and commanded him to enter the ark.

medium.question: In the phrase “every thing that is in the earth shall die,” what does “die” mean?
answers: Grow
Escape
Perish
medium.explanation: The word means to die or perish; the context refers to death caused by the flood.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, from under heaven”?
answers: The judgment is described as affecting all living creatures on earth
The judgment affected only Noah and his family
The judgment affected only creatures living in water
challenge.explanation: The phrase broadens the description to every living creature under heaven.

challenge.question: What was the role of the covenant mentioned before entering the ark?
answers: To promise that there would never be a flood
To emphasize God’s special relationship and protection for Noah during the flood
To promise that everyone would enter the ark
challenge.explanation: The covenant distinguishes Noah and his family within the judgment and expresses God’s special protection.

challenge.question: To whom does the Lord speak directly in the words “with thee will I establish my covenant”?
answers: To Noah’s sons
To everyone on earth
To Noah
challenge.explanation: “With thee” is singular, so the covenant is addressed directly to Noah, even though his family enters with him.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, from under heaven”?
answers: The judgment is described as affecting all living creatures on earth
The judgment affected only Noah and his family
The judgment affected only creatures living in water
questions.explanation: The phrase broadens the description to every living creature under heaven.

questions.question: What was the role of the covenant mentioned before entering the ark?
answers: To promise that there would never be a flood
To emphasize God’s special relationship and protection for Noah during the flood
To promise that everyone would enter the ark
questions.explanation: The covenant distinguishes Noah and his family within the judgment and expresses God’s special protection.

questions.question: To whom does the Lord speak directly in the words “with thee will I establish my covenant”?
answers: To Noah’s sons
To everyone on earth
To Noah
questions.explanation: “With thee” is singular, so the covenant is addressed directly to Noah, even though his family enters with him.

paragraphs.title: The Animals Saved in the Ark

easy.question: Who was required to bring the animals into the ark?
answers: Noah
Abraham
Moses
easy.explanation: The command to bring the animals into the ark was given to Noah.

easy.question: How many animals of each kind were to enter the ark?
answers: One
Two
Ten
easy.explanation: The verse says, “two of every sort.”

easy.question: What was to be included in each pair?
answers: Two males
Two females
A male and a female
easy.explanation: The verse says, “they shall be male and female.”

medium.question: Why were a male and a female of each kind brought into the ark?
answers: So they could reproduce after the flood
So they could guard the ark
So they could provide food for Noah
medium.explanation: A male and a female could produce offspring, allowing each kind to continue afterward.

medium.question: Which list matches the kinds of animals mentioned in the verse?
answers: Fish, wild animals, and human beings
Fowl, cattle, and creeping things of the earth
Angels, birds, and fish
medium.explanation: The verse mentions fowl, cattle, and every creeping thing of the earth.

medium.question: What does the phrase “after their kind” mean in “of fowls after their kind”?
answers: According to their kind
Beside their home
Very quickly
medium.explanation: The phrase means according to each animal’s kind or species.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “of every living thing of all flesh” and the following list?
answers: Only cattle entered the ark
Only animals that lived in water entered
The rescue included many kinds of animals
challenge.explanation: The general statement is followed by birds, cattle, and creeping things, showing the wide range of animals included.

challenge.question: Why does the verse repeat the phrase “after their kind”?
answers: To emphasize that each kind was preserved separately
To say that all animals were the same size
To indicate that only females entered
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the animals were brought according to their different kinds.

challenge.question: What relationship between verses 19 and 20 is especially clear?
answers: Verse 20 cancels the command in verse 19
Verse 20 specifies the groups included in the general command
Verse 20 speaks only about human beings
challenge.explanation: Verse 19 gives the general rule of two from each kind, and verse 20 lists the groups: birds, cattle, and creeping things.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “of every living thing of all flesh” and the following list?
answers: Only cattle entered the ark
Only animals that lived in water entered
The rescue included many kinds of animals
questions.explanation: The general statement is followed by birds, cattle, and creeping things, showing the wide range of animals included.

questions.question: Why does the verse repeat the phrase “after their kind”?
answers: To emphasize that each kind was preserved separately
To say that all animals were the same size
To indicate that only females entered
questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the animals were brought according to their different kinds.

questions.question: What relationship between verses 19 and 20 is especially clear?
answers: Verse 20 cancels the command in verse 19
Verse 20 specifies the groups included in the general command
Verse 20 speaks only about human beings
questions.explanation: Verse 19 gives the general rule of two from each kind, and verse 20 lists the groups: birds, cattle, and creeping things.

easy.question: What did God command Noah to take?
answers: Every kind of food that could be eaten
Only water
Only wood
easy.explanation: God told Noah to take every kind of food that could be eaten.

easy.question: Who was the food for?
answers: Only God
Noah and the others with him
Only Noah
easy.explanation: The verse says it would be food for Noah and for them.

easy.question: What did Noah do after receiving the command?
answers: He asked many questions
He left the ark
He did everything God commanded him
easy.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Noah did according to all that God commanded him.

medium.question: Why did Noah have to gather food?
answers: So Noah and those with him would have food to eat
To sell it
To build the ark with it
medium.explanation: The food was gathered to provide nourishment for Noah and everyone with him.

medium.question: In the phrase “thou shalt gather it to thee,” what does “gather” mean?
answers: Throw away
Collect
Hide
medium.explanation: The word means to collect or bring together the food.

medium.question: What order of events is described in these verses?
answers: Noah ate, then received the command, and finally gathered food
Noah built the ark, left it, and finally received food
God commanded Noah to gather food, and Noah did as he was commanded
medium.explanation: The command to gather food comes first, followed by the statement that Noah obeyed it.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “according to all that God commanded him, so did he”?
answers: Noah obeyed completely
Noah did not understand the command
Noah carried out only part of the command
challenge.explanation: The repetition between “all that God commanded” and “so did he” emphasizes Noah’s complete obedience.

challenge.question: What does “it shall be for food for thee, and for them” show about the purpose of the food?
answers: It was intended only for Noah
It was intended for Noah and others
It was intended only for the others
challenge.explanation: The words “for thee, and for them” identify Noah and another group as its recipients.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the wording “of all food that is eaten”?
answers: Noah had to take only one food
Noah had to take only sweet food
Noah had to prepare a variety of edible foods
challenge.explanation: “All food that is eaten” indicates a supply of different kinds of suitable food.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “according to all that God commanded him, so did he”?
answers: Noah obeyed completely
Noah did not understand the command
Noah carried out only part of the command
questions.explanation: The repetition between “all that God commanded” and “so did he” emphasizes Noah’s complete obedience.

questions.question: What does “it shall be for food for thee, and for them” show about the purpose of the food?
answers: It was intended only for Noah
It was intended for Noah and others
It was intended only for the others
questions.explanation: The words “for thee, and for them” identify Noah and another group as its recipients.

questions.question: What can be understood from the wording “of all food that is eaten”?
answers: Noah had to take only one food
Noah had to take only sweet food
Noah had to prepare a variety of edible foods
questions.explanation: “All food that is eaten” indicates a supply of different kinds of suitable food.
